target_customer: Trucking fleets and owner operators that buy fuel and need payments and credit
problem: Trucking payments ran on outdated fuel cards with hidden fees and fraud exposure, and small fleets were poorly served.
business_model: Interchange and fuel discount economics on a fleet fuel card, plus payments and credit products
product_category: Fintech, transportation payments and fuel cards

founders.name: Vignan Velivela
founders.background_notes: Prior employers and education not found in sources opened. A FreightWaves speaker bio says he and co-founders met drivers at truck stops, but the co-founders are not named.

competitors.name: WEX
competitors.what: Long dominant fleet fuel card and payments provider

competitors.name: Fleetcor
competitors.what: Long dominant fleet fuel card provider including Fuelman and Comdata

technical_complexity.rationale: Card issuing, fraud controls and telematics linkage rely on partner banks and networks. The hard parts were underwriting credit and fraud, not core software.

defensibility.rationale: Card networks, bank partners and fleet data give some lock in, but rivals sold similar cards and AtoB moved between Visa and Mastercard.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: WEX and Fleetcor stayed independent rivals. No acquisition or copycat takeover was found through 2025.

market_need_then: Fuel is a large cost for fleets, and incumbents were criticized for fees and acceptance limits. The company says a zero fee card accepted anywhere addressed that pain.

branding.domain_note: atob.com is the company domain; how it was acquired was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions itself as Stripe for transportation, modern and fee transparent

branding.brand_signature: Stripe for Transportation positioning and the zero fee fuel card

brand_strength.rationale: Partnerships with Uber Freight, Murphy USA and Geotab point to recognition in trucking, per the YC page news list. No fan or merch evidence found.

outcome_analysis: AtoB sold a zero fee fuel card to a large trucking market dominated by WEX and Fleetcor. It raised a $155M Series B in August 2022 and $130M in September 2024, and signed distribution deals with Uber Freight, Murphy USA and others. It was still active with 75 staff. Growth looks driven by a clear customer pain and partner channels, though much of the capital includes debt and the early rounds are not verified.
notes: The Business Wire Series B page returned 403 to the fetch tool; the $155M figure comes from the headline in search results and PYMNTS, and the $230M total debt and equity statement comes from the same release as reported in search. Whether $155M is all equity is unclear. A $130M Sep 2024 raise is listed on the YC page news and Business Wire headline, with an aggregator calling it Series C; stage kept as other because no opened source states it. Aggregators gave conflicting earlier rounds (seed $2M Aug 2020 led by Bloomberg Beta; Series A $25M or Series B $75M in 2021), all single source and unverified. Banking Dive said $112M equity raised. Competitor sources are dated 2022, about two years after the batch; the incumbents existed long before. Name origin not found in search.
